spec_notes: docs/shiploop/spec.md (R-1 to R-5) restates the request but omits several stated points: that IllegalMoveError is an exported class (S-17), castling never out of or through check (S-22, S-23; only the general 'reject moves exposing or leaving one's king in check', which covers castling into check) and the e1g1/e1c1/e8g8/e8c8 castling notation (S-25); the code and tests have them anyway, and architecture.md AD-1 mentions castling start and transit squares. R-1 decides the invalid-input question in an ordinary line, 'The input contract is valid orthodox FEN', without marking it as the builder's choice or telling the customer, and the code follows it by not validating at all, so malformed FENs get confident answers (U-1). R-2 pins 'sorted lowercase UCI' and R-3 'legal UCI input', deciding strict move parsing (U-3) unmarked. R-4 decides 'no additional draw statuses', which agrees with the request. Its 'S1-S11' references are the builder's own numbering, not the inventory's.
tests_notes: All tests use only the public API. Several tests cover many behaviours at once: TC-2 both mates plus checkmate status and empty move lists; TC-3 (first) four castles plus three rights-loss cases; TC-5 promotion generation, application for both colours and ten malformed/illegal moves; TC-6 stalemate, check replies and a pin. assert.throws(fn, IllegalMoveError) degrades to 'throws anything' if the export disappears (S-17 proof: suite stays green), so the exported-class requirement is not guarded. TC-8 is wall-clock timing (performance.now) and measures the middlegame call after earlier tests have warmed the JIT; bounds are generous (observed 0.06 ms and 0.70 ms). TC-5 asserts that ' e2e4', 'a7a8Q' and null throw IllegalMoveError, which would fail on another correct build that documents trimming or case-insensitive moves (inventory U-3 allows that) or throws TypeError for a non-string. Exact-FEN comparisons assume the canonical KQkq rights order, which any correct build should share. No test covers an invalid FEN.
maintainer: Legality and application share one move object (from, to, captureSquare, promotion, rookFrom/rookTo) and boardAfter on a 0x88 array; addCastles even fabricates a king move to test the transit square, so changing the move shape or board indexing ripples through attacked, legalCandidates, rightsAfter and applyMove at once. Adding FEN validation is the obvious next change and must be done in parseFen without breaking the whitespace tolerance and the BigInt counters, with no existing test to show what invalid input should do.
